mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at the decision time point reduces equity discount rates and stimulates economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through improved valuation metrics.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through elevated corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS (both rising in the past month) is followed by negative S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals potential monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is above 100.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls below 50,000 persons signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth is below 50, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP level (GDPC1 above 23500 billion) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST above 1500 thousand units) indicates robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through elevated corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint condition of GDPC1 > 23500 and HOUST > 1500 is followed by negative S&P 500 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) grow at a rate exceeding 0.5% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
